A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Slot Interpreter work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching content relocated or renamed in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, object-detection and CLEVrTex property-prediction experiments, together with ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original segmentation, retrieval and CLEVr-Hans classification experiments, while retaining object-detection results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core encoders, nearest-slot score aggregation, contrastive alignment and SET generator remain; the generator moves to Appendix E. v2 adds a downstream ViT consuming grounded slot tokens. It also reports revised objective weighting: contrastive/reconstruction coefficients change from 1/0.5 in v1 to 0.5/0.5 in v2.

E1.justification: v2 adds object-segmentation evaluation on the retained datasets and few-shot classification on CLEVr-Hans 3 and 7, including transfer from a CLEVrTex-trained tokenizer. Retrieval and MOVi-C/COCO detection remain, but the CLEVrTex property-prediction task from v1 Appendix A.5.1 is removed.

E2.justification: Retrieval adds CLIP and removes Vanilla Slot Attention, although Vanilla remains in detection. Ungrounded slots and HMC matching correspond to the earlier DINOSAUR and DINOSAUR-FT comparisons; the renamed NSI ablations also remain. The new classification comparison evaluates patch tokens and CoSA alongside ungrounded and NSI tokenizers.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FG-ARI and mBO segmentation evaluation with shared-backbone/compute controls, plus 100-shot, 1000-shot and full-data classification and annotation-budget sweeps. Retrieval drops R@10 and mean rank. Existing dataset splits remain unchanged, but the reported contrastive/reconstruction loss balance changes; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds segmentation and retrieval slot-count sweeps, category-versus-bounding-box ablations, grounding-annotation sensitivity, classification confusion matrices, attention-depth analyses and misleading-rationale cases. These investigate questions beyond v1's backbone/context ablations and detection slot-count analysis. Existing t-SNE and slot-search analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use standard deviations over five seeds, including the same less-than-0.3 reporting convention for retrieval. v2 extends this practice to new experiments without introducing a different run-count policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds segmentation, classification, CLIP retrieval and ablation results while removing CLEVrTex property-prediction and several retrieval entries. The retained detection sweep also has revised values: DINOSAUR-FT at 20 slots is approximately 15% AP50 in v1 Fig. 8 versus 3% in v2 Fig. 39. These are revised reported results, not an established controlled cross-version performance change.

T1.justification: The slot-attention, nearest-slot/max-sum alignment, contrastive probability and SET/Hungarian formulations are retained, largely with combined notation and renumbering. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation appears; the revised loss coefficients concern training configuration.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on grounding and generating visual programs for retrieval, detection and property prediction. v2 foregrounds a grounding/co-training paradigm and adds central claims about improved object discovery and efficient few-shot reasoning using grounded slot tokens. Generation remains in the appendix but loses its former prominence.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses about symmetry breaking and semantic-class grouping, interpretations of CLIP limitations and cross-dataset grounding transfer, and discussion of annotation requirements. Appendix D.3 qualifies interpretability through classification errors and correct predictions supported by incorrect or ambiguous slots, substantially extending v1's alignment/generation interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously unstated broadcast-decoder dimensions, the two-layer ViT configuration and CLEVr-Hans hyperparameters and budgets. Conversely, v1's dedicated Vanilla Slot Attention configuration table and DINO weight-source link disappear. Most existing NSI and generator implementation information remains available.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around symbol grounding and visual tokenization, adding a Visual Tokenizers subsection and discussion of CoSA, CLIP and several tokenizer families. The earlier general set-prediction/object-detection discussion and associated citations are removed. This changes the research context beyond bibliographic or terminology edits.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and 'program' terminology becomes 'schema.' The main narrative is reorganized around discovery, grounding and reasoning; generator/detection material moves to Appendix E. The appendices are reorganized and gain a contents page.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 adds overview and architecture diagrams, replaces the retrieval table with combined bar-chart/correspondence panels, and adds segmentation, classification, confusion-matrix and rationale displays. Retained detection figures are redrawn and relocated, while the CLEVrTex property-prediction plot disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's retrieval/detection focus: controlled segmentation tests assess representation quality, while confounded classification, transfer and annotation-budget experiments test downstream reasoning and practical supervision needs. Explicit rationale failures also qualify interpretability. These gains outweigh the loss of CLEVrTex property-prediction results and detailed retrieval entries, although the revised detection baseline curve lacks an explanation.
